test_title: PYST 14: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - English Language (Held On 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
What is the active voice of the following sentence?

When was America discovered by Columbus and later it was renamed after Amerigo Vespucci?

options.text: When was Columbus discovered America and later they had renamed it after Amerigo Vespucci?
When Columbus discovers America and later who renamed it after Amerigo Vespucci?
When did Columbus discover America and later they renamed it after Amerigo Vespucci?
When Columbus discovered America and later he were renamed after Amerigo Vespucci?

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Active voice structure: The subject (the doer) performs the action, followed by the verb and the object.
 
• In the passive voice, the sentence is: "When **was America discovered by Columbus** and later **it was renamed** after Amerigo Vespucci?"
 
• Both parts of the sentence are in the **Past Simple** tense.
 
• **First part:** The passive "was [subject] discovered by [agent]" becomes the active interrogative "did [subject] discover [object]." Thus, "When was America discovered by Columbus" becomes "When **did Columbus discover** America."
 
• **Second part:** The passive "it was renamed" has an implied agent (people/they). In active voice, we use "they renamed it."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"When did Columbus discover America and later they renamed it after Amerigo Vespucci?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"When was Columbus discovered America..." – Incorrect because "was... discovered" here is grammatically disjointed and incorrectly suggests Columbus was being discovered.
 
• **Option 2: **"When Columbus discovers..." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to Present Simple.
 
• **Option 4: **"...he were renamed..." – Incorrect due to subject-verb disagreement ("he were" is wrong) and it lacks the proper interrogative structure for the first clause.
